playbook:
When asked to hide at the start of the patrol, pick a central cell (around 4–6) to balance coverage and hit probability.

When later rounds narrow options or I’ve been missed repeatedly, shift to a low-probability corner (7–9 or 1–3) to break predictable patterns.

When posting a station note, keep it short, neutral, and non-informative: one sentence that signals readiness but reveals nothing about my hide or intent.

When the standing order directs me to fire at the next live station, follow the standing order (do not skip or substitute targets) unless a clear tactical reason to break order is presented.

When I fire, pick a cell consistent with my most recent hide moves (if I hid center, favor mid cells; if I moved corner, favor that corner) to maximize chance that my shot matches a true target if someone is shooting toward me.

When I am told the private result of my shot, always file the matching public claim (truthful claims only).

When choosing an escort claim, name another live player-boat only (never name a non-boat or neutral entity). Do not claim escorts for non-players; that is invalid and useless.

When considering mutual escort deals, only name a boat if I reasonably expect the other to reciprocate (mutual naming yields 5 points each); do not unilaterally claim escorts unless it benefits a clear alliance.

When Harbor is on the board, never fire on Harbor (the penalty is applied to the shooter and is not worth provoking Harbor’s jettison rule).

When shots have repeatedly missed a single target over several rounds, adjust my aiming pattern rather than repeating the same cell: repetition did not work.

When I score a hit, maintain the approach that led to it for at least one more round (hits indicate a correct pattern), then vary to avoid being predictable.

When in doubt about where others are hiding, default to center for the first shot and then explore edges in subsequent shots.

When writing notes or claims, avoid making commitments that would obligate me to reciprocate escort claims or expose my hide; keep communications functional, not strategic unless I have a negotiated alliance.

1.text:
When given hide choice, I vary my cell; avoid always hiding in the same obvious central cell (do not default to 5 every round).

When I have been targeted recently by a specific opponent, I move off the spots they used most recently.

When posting a station note, keep it non-committal and uninformative (short status, no coordinates or intentions) unless I have an explicit deal to coordinate escorts or mutual points.

When the standing order tells me which station to fire at, I fire at that named boat unless there is a tactical reason not to (see Harbor rule below).

When choosing a firing cell, do not reuse the same cell every round; randomize within a constrained set so I am not trivially predictable.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I file the claim exactly as required (claim must equal private result) — never invent or invert claim.

When considering escort claims, do not claim an escort unless I have a clear mutual agreement with another boat; only claim an escort if I expect the other boat to name me as well (mutual naming yields 5 points each). If no agreement, claim none.

When Harbor is the target, do not fire on Harbor unless the gain (3 points transferred) is worth inviting the picket-office threat and possible retaliation; treat Harbor as effectively off-limits by default.

When I score a hit on another boat, I expect their behavior to change (retaliation or hiding change) and immediately adjust my hide and firing pattern next round.

When I am repeatedly missed by everyone, do not assume safety — vary hiding and firing strategy to try to generate hits rather than staying passive.

When coordinating for mutual escort points, set the agreement in clear station notes and confirm before the round ends; if the other party does not reciprocate, do not persist in unilateral claims.

When I feel pressured or singled out, prioritize evasive hiding over aggressive, repeatable firing choices.

When a choice clearly failed previously (being predictably central or firing the same cell every round), stop that behavior and adopt variability.

2.text:
When told to hide at the start of a round, pick a central cell (4–6) to balance chance of being shot and potential to hit others.

When I am shot in a previous round, change my hide to a cell not used by me recently (do not repeat the same hide twice in a row).

When selecting a hide late in the patrol (final rounds), shift toward edges (1–3 or 7–9) to reduce predictability after earlier central hides.

When posting my station note, keep it neutral and non-informative — use the team-standard phrase (e.g., "steady on station") unless I am coordinating an explicit escort agreement.

When the standing order says to fire at the next live station, follow the standing order and aim at that boat.

When choosing a firing cell under the standing order, vary the numeric offset each round (don’t fire the same cell repeatedly); mix central and edge numbers so my pattern is hard to exploit.

When the office privately tells me the true shot result, file the required public claim truthfully (claim hit if told hit, claim miss if told miss).

When considering escort claims, do not claim an escort unless I can secure a mutual naming; only claim an escort when I have reason to expect the named boat will name me back (mutual naming yields +5 each).

When I cannot secure a mutual escort, file [salvage: none] rather than make a solitary escort claim for no return.

When Harbor is in play, avoid firing on Harbor unless I accept the guaranteed jettison payoff and want to remove Harbor; do not shoot Harbor routinely because it creates major negative consequences from Harbor’s standing signal.

When coordinating or attempting deals, use station notes conservatively and only to set up explicit mutual escort agreements; do not reveal hide coordinates or shot intentions in notes.

When a targeted boat has been hit previously, prefer varying my shot choices (change cell selection strategy) rather than doubling down on previous misses.

When in doubt, prioritize consistent truthful claims and low-information notes over risky signaling that could expose my hide or enable others to exploit my pattern.
